summary: AAUW International Fellowships support women who are not U.S. citizens or permanent residents to study full time in a STEM field at a U.S. institution, working towards a first master's or a first academic or professional doctorate. The programme has run since 1917 and the awards go to women who plan to use their expertise in their home countries or communities. A limited number of awards are for study in a country other than the applicant's own. The 2027-28 round closed on 17 September 2026.
eligibility_notes:
You must identify as a woman and be a non-U.S. citizen. U.S. permanent residents and green card applicants are not eligible, whatever their other citizenship.

You must be admitted to, or enrolled in, a first master's degree or a first academic or professional doctorate in a STEM field (the degree programme's own classification decides, not your research topic). Admission to at least one programme is required when you apply. Anyone who already holds a master's cannot apply for the master's award, and anyone who already holds a doctorate cannot apply for the doctoral award.

You need a degree equivalent to a U.S. bachelor's degree and a cumulative GPA of at least 3.5 on a 4.0 scale for your highest degree earned (a 3.49 is not eligible).

You must study full time at a U.S. Department of Education-accredited institution; part-time study is not eligible. Foreign branches of U.S. institutions count as outside the U.S. The programme must start on or before 15 September 2027 and end on or after 30 April 2028. You must live in the U.S. or your study country for the whole fellowship period.

Study in a third country (neither the U.S. nor your home country) is considered only if your country of citizenship is under a U.S. travel ban and you cannot get a U.S. student visa, or if you are a Graduate Women International (GWI) member and your country is not under a ban.

You may apply for one degree type and one field only; applying for master's and doctorate together, or in two fields, is not allowed. If your degree title differs from the chosen field, explain this in the application. Deferred admission to 2027-28 is eligible if the new start date is on or before 1 September 2027 and the end date is on or after 30 April 2028.

Not eligible: current AAUW Board members, employees (including temporary staff, consultants, interns and contractors), current AAUW review panelists, their immediate family, and previous AAUW fellowship or grant recipients (Community Action Grants and branch or local awards are excluded from this rule). Applicants who cannot return home for humanitarian or other serious reasons are still considered, based on their links to their home or current communities.
age_experience_notes: No age limit and no work-experience requirement is stated.
funding_summary: A one-time stipend of US$20,000 for master's fellows and US$25,000 for doctoral fellows, paid to the fellow only in two equal payments (at the start and at the midpoint of the term). Awards cannot be renewed. Allowed uses include tuition, fees, required course materials, housing, food and dependent care. Not allowed: research assistants, expenses already incurred or personal loan repayment, publication costs, institutional overhead and tuition for dependents.
programmes_note: Any full-time STEM master's or doctoral programme counts, judged by the programme's STEM classification (AAUW uses the DHS STEM Designated Degree Program List). Eligible categories in the AAUW field list: life and biological sciences, physical sciences, earth, environmental and space sciences, health and medical sciences (STEM-based), computer, data and information sciences, core and specialised engineering, mathematics, and statistics and quantitative fields. Specified medical doctorates (MD, DO, DDS, DMD, OD, DC, DPM, PharmD, DVM) are also listed as eligible. Applicants may list up to five programmes in the application.
institutions_note: Any U.S. Department of Education-accredited institution in the United States. Foreign branches of U.S. institutions count as study outside the U.S. and are only possible under the third-country rules. Recipients must enrol in the programme and institution named in the application; changing discipline, programme type or institution leads to disqualification (the exception is for applicants from a travel-ban country who cannot get a U.S. visa).

summary.detail: First master's degree in a STEM field, full time, at a U.S. accredited institution. Stipend US$20,000 in two equal payments. Programme must start by 15 September 2027 and end on or after 30 April 2028. Assessed on academic or scholarly excellence, feasibility of the plan, commitment to women and girls at home, long-term STEM career objectives and impact, and the strength of the financial plan.

benefits.conditions: One-time award, not renewable. Paid to the fellow only, in two equal payments at the start and at the midpoint of the term (first stipend July to September 2027, second December 2027 or January 2028). Tax is withheld, usually at 14% or 30%, for foreign persons studying in the U.S.

benefits.limit_text: Tuition and fees may be paid from the stipend
benefits.conditions: The stipend is not paid to the university. Allowed uses: tuition, fees, required course materials, housing, food and dependent care.

benefits.limit_text: Housing may be paid from the stipend
benefits.conditions: Part of the single stipend, not a separate benefit.

benefits.limit_text: Research assistants, earlier expenses or personal loan repayment, publication costs, institutional overhead and tuition for dependents
benefits.conditions: These are prohibited uses of the stipend.
Visas are the fellow's sole responsibility. AAUW does not sponsor visas or help with J-1 waivers, though the award letter may be used in a visa application.
The pages read do not list travel or insurance as separate components.

requirements.text: Narrative application, submitted in the AAUW Fellowships & Grants application portal. AI tools may help, but the work must reflect your own ideas and voice.

Two letters of recommendation, requested through personalised online links sent to the referees' professional email addresses. Dossier services (Parment, Interfolio) are not accepted and form letters are discouraged.

Proof of degrees: diplomas or official transcripts showing conferral and date. Foreign-language documents need translations, with a certified translation for the highest degree. Equivalency to a U.S. bachelor's may need an institutional explanation or a credential evaluation (WES, ECE or another NACES member).
Official transcripts for all degree programmes, listing courses and grades. Certified translations are required for the highest degree.

Proof of cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale for the highest degree (minimum 3.5). If the grading system is not 4.0, supply an official conversion or a credential evaluation with a detailed grade list. Scholaro's GPA Calculator is an accepted conversion tool.

Proof of English proficiency. Accepted scores: TOEFL iBT 79, TOEFL Essentials 8.5, revised TOEFL paper 60, IELTS 6.5, Cambridge 176, Duolingo 120. Other options: a statement as a native English speaker, or transcripts showing English-medium instruction. Institutional TOEFL scores are not accepted. TOEFL, IELTS and Duolingo scores are valid for two years; Cambridge scores do not expire.
Proof of admission (admission letter with start date, plus deferral approval if applicable) or enrolment verification.
Proof of Graduate Women International (GWI) membership.
requirements.conditional_rule: only if studying outside both the U.S. and your home country (and your home country is not under a U.S. travel ban)

application_steps.title: Check eligibility and gather your documents
application_steps.detail: Confirm you are a woman, a non-U.S. citizen and not a permanent resident, with admission to a first full-time STEM master's or doctorate that starts by 15 September 2027. Prepare the narrative, proof of degrees, transcripts, GPA proof (at least 3.5), English proof and proof of admission or enrolment. The AAUW help centre and information sessions are available for questions.

application_steps.title: Apply in the AAUW application portal
application_steps.detail: Create an account in the AAUW Fellowships & Grants application portal and complete the narrative application. You may list up to five programmes, but only one degree type and one field. Invite two referees from the portal; they get an online link at a professional email address. The 2027-28 window ran from 17 August 2026 (9:00am ET) to 17 September 2026 (5:00pm ET). Incomplete applications are not considered.

application_steps.title: Completeness and eligibility check
application_steps.detail: AAUW's Fellowships & Grants team first checks that each application is complete and eligible.

application_steps.title: Panel review by STEM scholars
application_steps.detail: Eligible applications go to an independent panel of STEM scholars that meets once a year. Master's and doctoral applicants are both judged on academic or scholarly excellence, feasibility of the plan, commitment to women and girls in the home country or community, long-term STEM career objectives and impact, and the strength and feasibility of the financial plan; doctoral applicants are also judged on the originality and potential contribution of the work. Where merit is comparable, preference may go to applicants from countries with low past representation, first international academic experience, living in the home country at application, first-generation graduates, single-parent households, caregivers (including pregnancy), and students at R2 institutions or those with limited research resources.

application_steps.title: Awards decided and announced in March 2027
application_steps.detail: Awards depend on the panel's recommendations, available funds and final AAUW approval. Award notification is in March 2027 and AAUW gives no early notice before 15 March. Award status is final only after all acceptance materials are received and approved.

application_steps.title: Accept the award and submit tax forms
application_steps.detail: Foreign persons studying in the U.S. submit Form W-8BEN; withholding is 14% for F, J, M or Q visa holders (or the treaty rate) and 30% otherwise or with no tax ID, and AAUW recommends applying early for a U.S. ITIN or SSN. Foreign persons studying and living outside the U.S. need no tax form and have no withholding. U.S. persons submit Form W-9. AAUW sends a 1042-S by 15 March each year and does not give tax advice.

application_steps.title: Receive the stipend in two payments
application_steps.detail: The first stipend is paid July to September 2027 and the second December 2027 or January 2028. The money goes to the fellow only. You must begin or continue the programme by 15 September 2027 and finish no earlier than 30 April 2028, with no exceptions.

application_steps.title: Stay in your programme, arrange your visa and report
application_steps.detail: You must stay in the listed programme and institution; a change of discipline, programme type or institution leads to disqualification. Arranging a visa is your own responsibility. Research outside your study country is allowed if it does not cause an absence of roughly six months. A mid-year report is due in December 2027 and the final report by 31 July 2028. Report any change of tax status to the programme officer promptly.
